text_fidelity_a:
Thames & Kosmos Drop It | Super Fun Family Strategy Game | Parents' Choice Silver Award Winner, Multi-Color Drop It is a simple game - you drop shapes into a Plinko-like contraption,, and depending on what happens when they fall, you earn points, so long as you follow some simple placement rules - you cannot touch the same shapes or colors, and the edges have restrictions on what shapes can touch them. It's so simple, and yet it's incredibly fun.

Not only is this a fun game though, it's a game that really teaches young players how to formulate an argument, identify problems with shape placement, and think about how and what to play. I played with a five-year-old who has no strategic ability yet, but who was able to, after just one play, identify if a shape was correctly placed right away and push forward with better strategy in her second game. The older child was better able to adapt, but also showed great ability to arrange and save her shapes for times when they'd be advantageous for use.

My one concern with this game is that it is quite a bit more difficult with three players, since that is the player count in which only three of the four colors are in use, and it's harder to place pieces. This is easily remedied by a simple rules change.

This is one of the best kids games I've ever played, and far and away one of the best games I've played recently. Get it.
text_fidelity_b: Thames & Kosmos Drop It | Super Fun Family Strategy Game | Parents' Choice Silver Award Winner, Multi-Color

Prime Climb Great game for helping kids understand factors and learn their multiplication/division (and addition/subtraction) facts, plus it's FUN! The part that initially drew me in for where my kids are was the color coding of the basic primes, and by extension the use of those colors to represent factors in the products. Then, it arrived and the gameplay was really fun--there are two ten sided dice and you can add, subtract, multiply or divide the number you are on by each die in turn to move. If you land on a prime you get to draw a Prime Card, which you can either use right away or save for later to benefit yourself or target an opponent, depending on whether the card is an Action card or Keeper. The first person to move both pawns to 101 wins. If you get tired of the standard rules, though, they apparently have some variations here: [...] but I have not yet tried any--looking forward to doing so after we've played through a few more times.

Oh and keep in mind that it takes longer the more players there are--folks with younger kids might want to keep it to 2 or 3 players so it doesn't go so long, or modify the rules so people don't get sent back to start so often. I'm sure there are cooperative ways to play too if that's more up someone's alley, like it was for us when the kids were younger.
text_fidelity_b: Prime Climb

Melissa & Doug Children's Book - Poke-a-Dot: What’s Your Favorite Color (Board Book with Buttons to Pop) - Poke A Dot /Push Pop Book For Toddlers And Kids Ages 3+ Let me begin by saying I’m a retired early childhood teacher of 24 years and was always in search of books that were appealing to children and encouraged them to engage in the books. This book would be at the top of my list of desirable books for children approximately 1-3 years of age. The book has visual and tactile appeal with a predictable rhyming text to promote early literacy! Love the vivid colors on each page to encourage children to learn their basic color names. As a bonus children are encouraged to tap the patented “pop-a-tropic” buttons to achieve the ever popular “bubble wrap” popping sound as they count the creatures on each page.

To summarize, this book is well worth the purchase! Young children are encouraged to develop or improve their counting skills, color recognition, and vocabulary building skills as they listen to the predictable text and depress the buttons as they count each colored bee, sheep, pig, frog, whale, cat, crab and bear.
I am now blessed with a grandson 7 months old and even he enjoys the book as I name the colored creatures and tap and count each one on the page.

Crayola Oil Pastels Portfolio Series, Water Soluble, Colors may vary, 12 Count (52-3612) I tried the Crayola neon pastels first and then decided to get a bigger set so I bought the portfolio crayolas set and have included a picture of all 24 colors.
They are bright with a variety of colors including black and white. Crayola has never come across as a high-end brand, but in oil pastels they are highly regarded as some of the best, and I agree. If you watch some of the videos on YouTube about how to use oil pastels you will realize how great these are. You can also see comparison videos, and the crayola brand gets very high marks. Oil pastels don't make a mess unless you use your finger to blend them, and then your finger will be a big mess. But you can clean it with baby wipes or soap and water or lotion to get down into your skin if it's dry. You can use traditional rolled paper sticks for blending also. These come packaged neatly so you can keep them in their original slots in that packaging. Besides coloring with them you can also use a wet brush to blend them, and you can layer them on top of each other or blend them together with your finger. I have also seen them covered with a clear acrylic paint and then used again on top of that paint. You can see that on YouTube. These are an inexpensive way to enjoy yourself artistically and produce beautiful results just like painting when you add the water or vodka or a blender like turpenoid.
text_fidelity_b: Crayola Oil Pastels Portfolio Series, Water Soluble, Colors may vary, 12 Count (52-3612)

text_fidelity_a:
World Series of Yahtzee Board Games [[VIDEOID:9706f008dc0f922f2a22889963de0e00]] This is a digital, board-based game of Yahtzee. I think it's made to compete with [[ASIN:B0042ET8S0 Uno Attack Game]] and [[ASIN:B001G5431A Bunco]], and it is much more fun than both of those games. Sometimes making a classic into a digital version is a mistake, but the designers did an awesome job with this game.

It's still [[ASIN:B00000IWH6 Yahtzee]]. You still get five dice, and you have to match the classic Yahtzee combinations of Yahtzee (five of a kind), four of a kind, three of a kind, full house, small straight (sequence or run) and large straight. But, everybody plays at once with their own sets of five dice, and the computer in the middle moderates everything, so goes very quickly and it's exciting.

The little buzzer in the middle is pretty sophisticated for a simple computer. It records who buzzes in and in which order you buzzed in, and it plays some fun countdown music. You get five seconds after the first person finishes to finish rolling and to buzz in yourself. Each person can collect up to one card per turn, based on what they rolled, but if you're not lucky, or if someone else gets your combination first, then you don't get any cards per turn. Usually turns take about thirty seconds each, and a full game all the way through will take about ten minutes, so it's very fast paced and fun.

I really liked the original Yahtzee, and I really like this too.

Pros:
+Very fun new version of an already fun classic
+Doesn't waste paper like the old version
+No more waiting around for slow players, like the old version
+You really should start playing this instead of Bunco, since there's a lot more strategy in this game
+You can roll the dice as many times as you want, where in traditional Yahtzee, you could only roll the dice three times per turn

Cons:
-The black dice with the red dots are so much cooler than the rest of the dice, so everyone will be fighting over these
-Made out of cheap plastic cardboard. If you love this game, which you probably will, and if you're not a dainty family, which you probably aren't, then you'll break these pretty quickly and go through about one of these games per year. It's still cheaper than a night at the movies, though, and this game is fun enough to justify getting a new one.
text_fidelity_b: World Series of Yahtzee Board Games

text_fidelity_a:
Thames & Kosmos Crystal Growing Science Kit Grow Over A Dozen Crystals with 15 Experiments, Includes Storage Case & 32 Page Color Laboratory Manual My child's science project last year was growing crystals. We had lots of fun using different temperature liquids, chemicals, etc. to see which would grow fastest, best, make the most solid of crystals and even made rock candy as a "take home" treat. I love the creativity of this kit. It allows for you to create UP TO 13 different experiments (but if you cheat you can get a couple more out of it). Some of the chemicals used are not safe for young kids so I'd highly suggest sticking to the recommended manufacturer's age. Not to mention the fact that some of the crystals will take longer than a week to fully form -- most kids don't have the patience to wait. Not waiting the proper amount of time to ensure the solidity of the crystals will result in disappointment as you can imagine something that isn't solid enough can break very easy. Following directions is paramount! Make sure you sit with your child and read through all of the instructions before beginning. I'd suggest sticking with the easiest project first to get their feet wet on experimenting then gradually go through the "harder" ones. I do like that the simple purchase of extra chemicals (or using sugar) can add a lot more fun to your kit. Thames & Kosmos is a good company. They even provide online printable instructions along side the greatly illustrated manual. http://www.thamesandkosmos.com/news/manualsamples/659127_glowingcrystals_manual_sample.pdf
The price of the kit is very fair. In fact, I'd say it would be an excellent science fair project to conduct with your child this spring. Start practicing now and wow the judges with modified versions. Just be sure to do your homework. Check out books from your local library on growing crystals and start taking notes. This could be a really fun learning experience for grade-schoolers and homeschoolers alike. The only thing I thought was slightly cheesy was the "treasure case" and the shapes (thus my four stars). But kids will get a kick out of them.
text_fidelity_b: Thames & Kosmos Crystal Growing Science Kit Grow Over A Dozen Crystals with 15 Experiments, Includes Storage Case & 32 Page Color Laboratory Manual

Fisher-Price Julius Jr. Rock 'n Playhouse Box Fisher Price knew what they were doing when they designed this Julius Jr. Rock'n Playhouse Box for ages 2 and up. The littlest children ages 2 and 3 years old just love it. The children really enjoy having Julius Jr. skateboard down the ramp and slide down the circular slide after going through a pie-shaped door.

They also love having Julius Jr. look through the telescope up on the rooftop and slide on the conveyor belt opening up the double doors where a Martian is ready for take-off in his space craft. But, their favorite thing is seeing the colorful dance floor light up and play music when Julius steps on it, as well as riding the elevator. There is even a disco ball attached to a weather vane upstairs that spins.

The elevator moves up to the second floor and rooftop, and with every floor, you hear Julius Jr. speak. He says things like, when he is looking out the window, What a beautiful day, I'm gonna need my sun hat. There are many sayings you will hear every time a bell rings at the floor stops, and they are different at times, so you will never know exactly what will be said.

This simple Playhouse is colorful and the pieces are made for little hands- easy to handle and nothing sharp. The Playhouse requires 2 AA batteries, which are included. You can also purchase extra Figure Packs, and you will want to, as Julius Jr. will have much more fun with a friend or two. Fisher Price has also made 2 more Playsets for Julius Jr. to play in- a Sortin' Sagebrush Farm and a Twirl-A-World Amusement Park. These sets will attach to this Playhouse making a world for Julius Jr. and your child to play in.

This 4 Star Rock'n Playhouse Box is a very simple set geared for the very young to enjoy with it's bright colors, sturdiness and simple moving parts. Two and three year olds especially love it.

First of all, the box is FULL of bricks., I dislike toys (or breakfast cereals!) that come in half-empty boxes. This is filled to the brim.

The treehouse set is not an easy set to build. Some parts of it are tricky, requiring gentle, patient hands.
Also, I have noticed in a few recent sets of things that I do not like. As I was building the bridge from one room to another, an essential piece was missing. It is LEGO, you can work around that sort of problem. In the last bag of the set, there was the missing piece. It was not needed on any of the steps for the last bag, it seems like it was "hidden" to frustrate me.

That said, when done it is simply beautiful. I built it with the fall leaves, and in spring, I will remove those and add the green leaves back!

Part of what makes this an advanced set is the physics of it. The small LEGO trunk should not be able to sustain the weight of the branches. However, some clever building techniques reinforce the trunk so it can easily carry the weight.

A spectacular build. Well worth the frustrations. A set to be enjoyed for many years to come!

Chongker Stuffed Animals Handmade Realistic Black Cat Plush Companion Pet Gifts for Women Birthday Anniversary Cat Lover I've answered a few questions about this, so I will include this right away- this is only a plush (a really nice one)- it has no mechanical parts. It doesn't purr, or "breathe", makes no kitten or cat sounds, and therefore, requires no batteries.

This item was purchased as an "emotional support plushie", if you will. People need companionship, even folks who are no longer able to care for a living pet (or no longer wish to have the heartbreak of losing a real cat).

This fellow can absolutely be mistaken for a real cat at a distance. While being held and stroked, it's close enough to pass for a cat who is less than bunny-soft. The expressions and eyes are amazing, the little toe beans are soft silicone and give a little when squeezed. I couldn't have asked for more detail.

The care that went into creating this plush is evident in the details- from the examples in the pictures and video to those included from customer reviews (and those of the custom plushies are OUTSTANDING, I may have to treat myself to one someday!). It comes in a reusable case (resembling a cat carrier) with a little care booklet and grooming tool.

Personally I wouldn't give this plush to a young child (especially not one of the long-haired ones)- frankly, I'd be worried they'd damage it (squish things in the fur, allow the fur to become matted, color it with markers, cut the whiskers or fur...). Kids can be amazingly accidently destructive at times (we know they don't mean to, it just happens).

For me, the Chongker plush was well worth the price for the comfort it brings. I am quite seriously considering purchasing a custom colored one. I've seen the quality in the base product, and I'm confident in their ability to create good lookalike.

text_fidelity_a:
Little Tikes Dozer Racer 2-in-1 Rc Vehicle for Kids UPDATE 10/10/18: The kids just love this RC car now that it works fine. It's frequently used by a 5-year-old boy and an 8-year-old girl, and it's holding up well to this heavy use. It is easy enough for the 5-year-old to work the controls, but entertaining enough for the 8-year-old to play with it with him. It doesn't run through the batteries as fast as I thought it would either.

UPDATE 9/18/18: I received the replacement toy, and it works perfectly. The toy is so fun and a good price for what you get. I wouldn't hesitate to buy one as a present in the future.

UPDATE 9/10/18: Yesterday (Sunday), I sent an e-mail to customer support about the malfunction. I received a reply early this morning. It was a real person who communicated clearly and actually addressed my problem. They're sending a replacement that has been tested to make sure it works fine. They're also sending a pre-paid return label for the return of the malfunctioning toy so their engineers can look at the unit. I'm super impressed.

ORIGINAL REVIEW (3 stars): This is generally such a fun, nice toy that I almost gave it 4 stars even though I would have returned this toy if I'd actually bought it. The remote is fairly simple: hold down the left button to turn left, hold down the right button to go right, hold both down to go forward. These button work great. But one of the transform buttons had a glitch from the beginning. The vehicle starts out as a race car when you turn it (and the remote) on. When you hit the bulldozer button, that transforms the race car into a bulldozer just fine every time. However, if the user likes to frequently switch back and forth between the two, the race car transform button will malfunction once out of every two or three times you hit it. When it malfunctions, instead of transforming into a race car, the bulldozer goes straight backward until it runs into something. Since there is no stop button, there is no way to stop the crash. You're no longer in control. At this point, the remote control commands do nothing, and you have to lift the vehicle to access the on/off switch to turn it off and on before it will work again. So far, it hasn't damaged the RC vehicle or anything else. However, this malfunction is a bother at the very least and will damage something eventually.

It's a cute toy that the kids really enjoy...as long as they don't transform often and crash every few minutes. The vehicle measures 10.5" long, 5.25" tall, and 7" wide. It requires 6 AA batteries--4 for the vehicle and 2 for the remote control. (Yes, we put brand new batteries in and tried another batch to see if the batteries were behind the problem. No improvement.) The toy is strong enough to push the box that it came in when in the bulldozer mode, and it can handle travel in a yard (at least when we tested it on a freshly mowed lawn). Intended for ages 3+. It certainly works well for the 5 year old boy who mainly plays with it. Made in China.
text_fidelity_b: Little Tikes Dozer Racer 2-in-1 Rc Vehicle for Kids

text_fidelity_a:
Boardwalk Arcade Pop-A-Shot This is video pinball as it used to be, before today's highly sophisticated physics simulators: floaty ball mechanics, dumbed down special features, bizarre flipper behavior, etc. Which is what I expected.

But I have to say, I'm impressed at the care they put into it nevertheless. They carefully reproduced the major playfield features and loops, the special modes, the multiballs, the spinning pizza. They made the marquee its whole own separate screen so they could have the interactive elements. They have a clever alternative for the plunger (hold down the button for longer to shoot harder). The flipper buttons on the side can get a little finger-cramping, so they put duplicates on the back of the unit so you can hold the whole unit. And, for better or for worse, they reproduced all of the boys' voices. Ugh. And unless I'm mistaken, unlike most of the Tiny Arcade series, it actually saves your high scores.

It's not all good - the "Start Game"/"Game Over" text is hilariously blocky, like an Atari 2600 game, and it pops up on the playfield. I don't know why they didn't put it on the marquee LCD where it belonged. The ball vibrates weirdly on the habitrails. A couple times, particularly in multiball, I've had the ball just simply fall through the hinge of the flipper. But these aren't huge concerns, and they're easily laughed off.

One warning for sensitive and/or young users: I've always thought the original pinball game's marquee's presentation of April was excessively sexy (she's a hero in her own right, not eye candy, darn it) but in the cut down version it looks like... uh, something else entirely.

All in all, this way exceeded my expectations. And it's actually quite fun! I'm not interested in the other "boardwalk arcade" games so far, but I'd gladly buy more pinball games like this one if they're at a similar level of playability.
text_fidelity_b: Boardwalk Arcade Pop-A-Shot

text_fidelity_a:
Fisher-Price Master Moves Mickey (M3) This is one cool Mickey! In fact, he's so cool his "ice cream doesn't melt"! (one of his cheesy phrases, not mine) Seriously, this has to be one of the coolest toys ever. Not only do both of my boys(16 months and 3 3/4 years) like it, but my husband and I love him, too. Whenever we have visitors, we have to pull this Mickey out, just to show him off. Sad, but true. One day, my 11 year old nephew was over here, and he even commented that this is the "coolest Mickey ever", and his little brother has the original dancing Mickey. I'm not familiar with the other dancing Mickeys, but apparently this one has more features.

My only complaint is the batteries, which really can't be helped with the kind of toy it is. This is more of simply a warning for you than a complaint. This Mickey really sucks the power out of batteries! He takes 6 AA batteries. He does come with a set, but they will wear off REALLY quickly. I would definitely have a high quality set of batteries waiting nearby. When the batteries get low, he will keep moving, but he won't be able to do the really fancy moves, like the handstand, and leg spins. Those are my favorite, so it's disappointing when I don't get to see those. ;)

To make him dance, all you have to do is press his nose. He will only do one set of dance moves and then he will tell you if you want to see more, just press his nose. He turns off pretty quickly. I'm sure this is so he won't use up the batteries even quicker. I like that he's smart, too. When he falls over, he asks for help getting up. When you help him up, he says, Thanks, pal!". There is an on/off switch on the back of his head. I have to make use of this switch when my youngest takes a nap.

Overall, if you don't mind the big investment price and the many batteries he will require, we HIGHLY recommend this Mickey!
text_fidelity_b: Fisher-Price Master Moves Mickey (M3)

LEGO NINJAGO Ninja Dragon Temple Set 71759 with Toy Motorcycle, Kai, NYA and Snake Warrior Minifigures, Gift for Kids 4 Plus Years Old LEGO have been hit by the inflation bug, and they've upped their prices recently on all sets. Nowhere is that more clear than in this set, which is very expensive for what you get.

Targeted towards the younger audience who is just beyond Duplo blocks, this is a pretty simple set with a pretty doofy-looking dragon that clearly skews younger, and doesn't fit in well with the rest of the Ninjago line, which is undoubtedly the LEGO line that has the highest "cool factor". So to judge this against a regular Ninjago set, this set woudl be a clear loser.

But it's really not for the older kids who can handle a ninja base or a 900-piece battle wagon, it's for littles. And for them, this is a fun set, but it is outrageously priced for what you get. It's essentially a few minifigs, a small dragon, a small set-piece, and a motorbike. Its simple to put together, but if you're working with a 4-year old, you probably need a little parental assistance.

For mini-munchkins, I suppose this would be a fun set to play with, but at close to $50 at the time of this writing, you are paying a very pretty penny for the fun you can have with it. At half that cost, and for the right audience, I'd find it a 4-star value. For what it is, I can't rank it higher than 3 stars.
text_fidelity_b: LEGO NINJAGO Ninja Dragon Temple Set 71759 with Toy Motorcycle, Kai, NYA and Snake Warrior Minifigures, Gift for Kids 4 Plus Years Old

Feleph Jungle Trees Building Blocks Bricks with 2 Base Plates (10 Inches for Each), Forest Garden Plants Flowers Bushes Animals Kit, Botanical Parts Scenery Toys Compatible with Major Brands LEGO would never make something like this. Sure, you can take their stuff and make anything with them, but too many of their kits make a definitive something. This is a definitive nothing, but a nothing that can entertain far beyond what a lot of different "somethings" can do.

LEGO is a toy, and this is often something that they remember to a fault. Here is a LEGO competitor, with bricks that are compatible, that remembers that it's not always a toy that kids want. They want an experience of playing, and that's what this Forest Garden kit gives them. Is it a dinosaur jungle? Is it a very nice tropical garden? Are the characters running from that alligator, or picnicing i the woods? With this, more than with any LEGO kit I've ever reviewed, there is a limitless number of possibilities.

There are no instructions with this kit, which is somewhat bothersome for the finnicky children who need a "right" way to put them together, but the playscape this provides is so unique that I can't give it less than 5 stars.

text_fidelity_a:
eeBoo French Flash Cards I had the great fortune of parents who made sure I learned three other languages as a kid. They started very early with me and I distinctly remember them making their own flashcards. It's too bad that they didn't have access to these beautiful, affordable, and very easy to use flashcards to aid them! Now, as a parent, teacher, and a nanny, I work hard to teach my kids the basics of French and Spanish, and I stumbled across these. They have been well worth the price and they were highly affordable. Best of all, my kids that I teach love the cards and enjoy using them too. I would recommend them to both the beginner and the advanced speaker as they embark on teaching others.

There are a few times that the cards use outdated pronunciations or word choices, but it's actually a plus in my book because it aids further in teaching. When I see a card with a different context of pronunciation or word choice than what is currently popular or commonly used, then I can supplement by saying "Or you could say it like this ..." text_fidelity_a: Nerf N-Strike Elite Firestrike This is my first external cocking blaster and I'm in awe of its range and accuracy.  Flat, in the house shots, are going from my kitchen, down the hall, and thru the family room and hitting the wall (45 feet!).  This is by far as well as my Rampage does. Accuracy is also superb.  I wasn't sure that such little cocking force was going to be able to shoot darts so far or fast.  This little gem will fire elite darts and whistlers.  It does not like streamlines and the suction cup darts.  The bullseye LED target light works pretty good in the dark, and seem to be accurate enough to nail a human size target at 30 feet.  I love the way the 2 spare dart holders seem to blend into the overall scheme of the blaster.  Hurray for nerf for attaching these to the packaging with easy to cut twine, rather than the usual zipties. text_fidelity_a:
Marvel Guardians of The Galaxy Big Blastin' Rocket Raccoon Figure, 10 Inch I'm going to review this not from the perspective of a toy, but rather as a piece of movie memorabilia. Years ago, I use to love to go to the local mall here in Austin and stop by the SunCoast Motion Picture Company store. Where you could buy all sort of movie related items as well as the movies themselves. Over the years I've bought a number of items very similar to this Rocket Raccoon figure for my collection. So when I was offered one of these 10 inch figure to check out I gladly accepted.

I wasn't expecting this figure to be so big - I knew it was suppose to be 10" but it seems bigger than that to me. It came in one of those open face boxes that allow you to actually touch the toy before taking it out of the box, and you can activate the sound effect as the item ships with the batteries already installed and the sound box is set in a demo mode. The sounds it make are pretty loud, they should put a smile on any child face (and a frown on any adults in the room).

Once out of the box, there is some assembly required. You have to pop the tail into the figures rear-end (yeah, I know). It takes some effort to do that, so I suggest having an adult do it. Other than that, the figure is ready to go. Like I mentioned there is a demo mode on the effects box. The effects are controlled with a three-position switch - Off, Try Me (demo), and On. The unit is powered by three double-A batteries which are located in the figures backpack (there is a screw securing the cover to the batteries). Once you turn on the power switch, there are two activation points - one on the figures leg and another on top of the gun he is holding. Pressing one or the other activates both motion and sound effects, plus the figure speaks phrases from the movie. The motion effects are just the end of the gun rotating and the figure shaking a bit. There are some light effects with the end of the gun & gun sight lighting up. There aren't that many spoken phrases - so they can get a bit repetitive after awhile.

The toy is pretty well made - a lot more substantial than most of the movie memorabilia, but then again it was made for kids to play with.

I kept the figure on my desk at work for about a week before bringing it home. I can't tell you how times people stopped and played with the figure (too many times, as that is what prompted me to finally take it home). I haven't seen the movie yet - but it is definitely one that I plan on seeing this summer.

I really like this figure - about the only thing I could comment on would be the detail of the end of his gun, everything else has a decent level of detail, but that part of the gun doesn't. Guessing that is more due to the fact that they made it out of clear plastic so that the light effect could be seen.
text_fidelity_b: Marvel Guardians of The Galaxy Big Blastin' Rocket Raccoon Figure, 10 Inch

text_fidelity_a:
Tokaido Board Game (Base Game) | Strategy Game | Travel Adventure Game | Exploration Game for Adults and Teens | Ages 8+ | 2-5 Players | Average Playtime 45 Minutes | Made by Funforge Simple, serene and elegant, this is a game like few others in your collection. This one is about a trip through Japan, and has very nice Japanese style artwork that really pops. One look at the box cover will tell you how elegant and evocative this game is, and that really is one of it's finest features.

Gameplay is rather simple. Those who rush ahead to see the sights first certainly get some kind of advantage - they often get first choice of where to go - while those who take their time will have plenty of opportunity to catch up, as the last player is always the next to move, meaning that travellers who venture too far out will allow others to make every stop along the way. There are "safe" and predictable options where you always get two or three points, and there are gambling options where you might be able to buy cards that give you far more.

It's a good, simple game that works well as a gateway game, but like many games, it says it's a decent two-player game, and I don't think that it is. It shines with three to four players. The decisions are not particularly deep or exciting, and much of the time, there really are only two choices that you can choose from - move really slow, or move really fast - and those choices are often easy to make.

If you're a gamer, I don't think you'll like this game. You can find better gateway games for sure, and there are thousands of games where you'll make more interesting choices. If you're just getting into games, or if you need something new to play with grandma, then this might be the best choice you can make.
text_fidelity_b: Tokaido Board Game (Base Game) | Strategy Game | Travel Adventure Game | Exploration Game for Adults and Teens | Ages 8+ | 2-5 Players | Average Playtime 45 Minutes | Made by Funforge

Educational Insights Hot Dots Let's Learn Kindergarten Math: Amazon Exclusive Kindergarten Math Workbook, Ages 5+ & Hot Dots Let's Master Grade 1 Reading with Talking Pen Very educational with great building-blocks for math success. The actual concepts focused in this activity book are great, but there are two areas of improvement outside of the lessons:

The Pen—My child tends to hold it in the middle or more toward the top, and the sound button always seems to get turned off. I don’t really know of a better placement for this button, but it’s worth mentioning. Maybe one of those slider buttons would be better at preventing the sound being turned off so easily.

The dots themselves don't seem very small, but still seem to cause us some issues when in use. Since the pen is quite large, my kiddo will often choose the right answer, put the pen down on the dot, but miss the dot slightly which then gives us a red light and a “sad” beep. Even though the answer is right, missing the dot makes you think that you’re wrong because you get the red light and sad sound. I then have to say “try that dot again” and reassure that the answer is correct. I do wish the dots were just a little bit larger to give the pen a broader area to make contact with the dot. It's not a major issue, as most of the time we do hit the dot just fine, but it's also something I've noticed that has happened several times.

Otherwise, these books are awesome, very educational and a lot of fun! More of 4.5 Stars for us.

Discover with Dr. Cool PRO Series Rock Tumbler - Turn Rocks into Stunning Gemstones! At first I put this in the kitchen, I quickly learned that it was too loud for an open floor plan, it made me listen to tv on too high of a volume, so when I switched to the 2nd grit I moved it to a spare bedroom. This worked out great since I go in that room almost daily I was able to keep up with knowing when to change out to the next grit.

This is super easy to set up and get started. It comes with absolutely everything needed to go from start to finish including jewelry items to use so you can show off your stones. The instructions are very easy to follow along too.It also comes with activity books and the jewelry pieces are a necklace, a ring, a keychain and ear rings.

The instructions gives you an idea of how long the stones should tumble in each grit and at what speed.
This is what I did..
-grit #1..I did for 3 days on #3 speed
-grit#2.. I started at 5 days on #2…then opened it up and decided it needed a few more days since they were a bit rough so I did 2
more days on #3 setting
-grit#3.. I did for 7 days on #1 setting.
-grit#4..I did 7 days on #1. The smaller stones were great , the larger stones had a few blemishes yet, but I like things when they
aren’t perfect so they were great for me…I will be making them into necklaces once I put holes in them.

As you can see from my pictures from start to finish how much the rocks changed. Then at the end I wiped them off with mineral oil as suggested in the instructions. This has been an amazing experience to watch the rough rocks transform into smooth beautiful stones.

text_fidelity_a:
Melissa & Doug Anteater Antics Action Game With 2 Plush Hats This is seriously one of the cutest games ever! I love the variety within it, too.

First of all, the anteaters themselves are very well made! You get two of them. Sometimes you get "masks" and they're pretty crappy, but these are quality. To wear these, there's two felt-like straps that will fit along the back of a child's head, along with velcro piece at the end of one strap. This means it will fit pretty much any child's head, because you can tighten or loosen as much of the strap as you want. There's another piece of velcro attached to the underside of the anteater's snout. This is what picks up the felt-like ants. Super, super cute!

Within this set is also the instructions, of course, along with a timer and a set of cards. These cards are similar to the cards within most matching games out there. We have several of them. They are small, square, and thick. One side of each of them simply shows an anteater at a picnic. The other side either shows various types of food for a matching game(This is also great for speech development!), or one or the other side of a colorful ant. This is also for matching, and a great way for the youngest players to learn colors. There are also a few "tummy ache" cards, which shows a sick anteater. A player will lose cards they've matched when this card comes into play.

You can really mix and match the various games in any way you want, especially depending on the ages involved. You can simply play "hide and seek" with the ants, or allow a player to find an ant once they find a match within the cards, or find the color of the ant they've matched together. You can add the timer for the older players or just to add a bit more challenge, if desired. You can also simply play a matching game with the cards for a quieter game. There are many possibilities for playing this game, so I imagine it will take longer to get "old" for most little ones.

Overall, this is a wonderful game, and one of the most fun ones we've had the pleasure of playing!
text_fidelity_b: Melissa & Doug Anteater Antics Action Game With 2 Plush Hats

text_fidelity_a:
Educational Insights Design & Drill Bolt Buddies Recycling Truck Toy, Take Apart Toy with Electric Drill Toy, STEM Toy, Gift for Boys & Girls, Ages 3+ The quality is great, and the concept is very creative. We play with this everyday, and think it’s fun, but there’s some thoughts I want to share:

-The clear bolts are somewhat difficult to find on the carpet. I wish the ends (tips) were colored to help make them stand out since they blend into the floor and surfaces.

-The drill bit is always falling out, and it’s also clear, so it can be hard to find it when it falls, and it’s cumbersome to have to keep putting it back in the drill repeatedly.

-The drill has two directions to tighten and loosen the bolts, which is adjusted with the sliding control. The drill itself works very well at tightening and loosening, but it gets a little involved helping my child make adjustments on the drill. My child wants to tighten and loosen a single bolt at a time before moving onto the next bolt, so we’re constantly flip-flopping the controls. Maybe slightly older preschoolers would be more independent using the drill, but I think a manual tool (like a screwdriver) would be the easiest to operate.

Our favorite part of this whole set is dropping all of the bolts in the back of the truck and then opening the hatch to watch all of them tumble out. My child thinks this is hilarious and is by far the best part!

In short, I think this whole set is a great concept, but is slightly overcomplicated. I really feel a simple screwdriver would help simplify the need to shift around buttons constantly, and would even help with dexterity and motor skills more than the cumbersome drill.
text_fidelity_b: Educational Insights Design & Drill Bolt Buddies Recycling Truck Toy, Take Apart Toy with Electric Drill Toy, STEM Toy, Gift for Boys & Girls, Ages 3+
